info.name: Traveler's Guide to Elysia
info.description: Songstress performer type for Aurora Builder.
info.author: Michael

description.p: Songstress. Songstresses possess the ultimate poise, refined by the songs they sing constantly. No songstress has ever failed to impress the people. They meet with their beauty, skill, and charm.
Additional Proficiencies. When you choose this performer type at 1st level, you gain proficiency with glaives, halberds, lances, and pikes.
Additionally, you gain proficiency in Persuasion. If you are already proficient in this skill, you gain expertise.

sheet.description: You gain proficiency with glaives, halberds, lances, and pikes. You also gain proficiency in Persuasion, or expertise if you already have it.

description.p: Singers Ear. When you choose this performer type at 1st level, you gain advantage on saving throws against being charmed.

sheet.description: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed.

description.p: Healing Descant. At 2nd level, a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier per short rest, you can use an action to sing a healing song.
All friendly creatures within 60 feet of you that can hear you regain 2d6 hit points. This healing increases at higher levels: 2d8 at 8th level, 2d10 at 13th level, and 4d10 at 17th level.
You can also use this ability more often at higher levels: +1 use at 8th level, +2 uses at 13th level, and +3 uses at 17th level.

sheet.description: Friendly creatures within 60 feet that can hear you regain 2d6 hit points. The healing improves at higher levels.

description.p: Inspiring Song. At 4th level, you can sing songs that give other creatures extra bravery in battle.
Harmony grants allies the ability to land critical hits on rolls of 19-20.

sheet.description: Harmony causes allies to score critical hits on rolls of 19-20.

description.p: Voice of Peace. At 6th level, your songs make creatures want to stop fighting.
As a bonus action, any enemies in range of your performance make all attacks with disadvantage. You can end this effect with a bonus action.
While you are singing this song, you have disadvantage on all Stealth checks. This only affects creatures that can hear you.
The range of your performance increases to 60 feet, and the target ally only has to be able to hear you.

sheet.description: Enemies in range of your performance that can hear you make attacks with disadvantage until you end the effect as a bonus action. While singing this song, you have disadvantage on Stealth checks. Your performance range becomes 60 feet, and target allies only need to hear you.

description.p: Soothing Song. At 8th level, your voice can penetrate the minds of any creature that can hear you.
As an action, you sing a beguiling song. All enemies within 60 feet of you that can hear you must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier).

On a failed save, a creature is incapacitated for 1 minute. Affected creatures make saving throws at the end of each of their turns. On a successful save, the creature is immune to the effects of this song for 24 hours.
This does not affect creatures that are immune to being charmed.

sheet.description: Enemies within 60 feet that can hear you make a Wisdom save or become incapacitated for up to 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of their turns. On a successful save, a creature is immune for 24 hours. This does not affect creatures immune to being charmed.

description.p: Perfect Pitch. At 10th level, your voice encourages others to heal.
Any creature within range of your performance regains additional hit points equal to your Charisma modifier whenever it receives healing.

sheet.description: Creatures within range of your performance regain additional hit points equal to your Charisma modifier whenever they receive healing.

description.p: Masterful Voice. At 13th level, you master your voice.
Your Inspiring Song now causes a critical hit on a roll of 18-20. Your Perfect Pitch now restores additional hit points equal to double your Charisma modifier.

sheet.description: Inspiring Song now causes critical hits on rolls of 18-20. Perfect Pitch now restores additional hit points equal to double your Charisma modifier.

description.p: Discordant Notes. At 17th level, you know how to use your voice to inflict pain on your enemies.

Twice per long rest, as an action, you can sing at one creature within 60 feet of you that can hear you. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier).

ul.li: On a failed save, the creature takes 6d8 psychic damage and is stunned until the end of your next turn.
On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and is not stunned.

description.p: This does not affect creatures immune to being charmed.

sheet.description: One creature within 60 feet that can hear you makes a Wisdom save or takes 6d8 psychic damage and is stunned until the end of your next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and is not stunned. This does not affect creatures immune to being charmed.

description.p: Diva. At 20th level, you achieve mastery as a songstress. No one else compares to your skills.
You gain an additional performance action, you have advantage on any Charisma checks made with your voice, and the range of your performance increases to 120 feet.

sheet.description: You gain an additional performance action, have advantage on Charisma checks made with your voice, and your performance range increases to 120 feet.
